about: Agent Behaviour Policy (ABP) for SovereignWebsite__Factory. CI reads this file on every run: a pipeline may take only the actions listed for it, an agent's commits may change only the paths listed for it, and every privilege held by the GitHub App or the AWS role is listed here with its reason. Anything not listed is refused. Changes to this file, to .github/ and to build/ take effect only when Dinis merges them.
source: Dinis, 19 November 2026 ~15:10 UTC in the conductor session recorded in team/keys.json: "let's take the opportunity to add as much automation (via CI pipelines) as possible, and then use our ABP to control it"; "let's try to do this completely from the CI pipeline and if we need to add more privs to the GH App and the AWS Role, we'll add them".

org-apply.note: A repository that exists but is not in org/repos.json is reported, never deleted. repo.seed only adds files that are missing on dev, never overwrites. pages.nudge_certificate re-sets the same custom domain only when Pages has no certificate or a failed one, so GitHub retries issuing it; it never runs while a certificate is pending.

org-apply.signers_note: Every seed carries .github/ci/signers.mjs and .github/workflows/signers.yml: each new commit on a site's dev is checked against the agent keys live in this repository's team/keys.json (an Agent: commit), or must be a commit GitHub verified (a person's); an "Owner override: <quote>, <where>" line is listed, not refused. New sites run it in pages.yml before the build, so a refused commit is not deployed. Sites already made get the two files from repo.seed (missing files only, nothing overwritten): there it turns the run red and names the commit; it blocks the deploy only once the keeper adds the step to the site's own pages.yml. Sites moved in by transfer are not seeded and do not get it. Source: incident board/incidents/2026-11-22__pushed-before-key-published.md, proposal 1; Dinis, 22 Nov 2026 ~15:30 UTC in factory.d's session: "Yes to the sign check. Yes to the org apply to the sites already there."

key-apply.note: A key request is keys/<date>__<id>/request.json, committed signed by a requester role; a security review and a counsel review (reviews_note). factory.d pushes both to dev without Dinis's merge; build/key-requests.mjs checks every rule, then adds the one entry to each target's team/keys.json on dev, in a commit signed by the factory key, citing the request and review commits. It never edits, retires or removes a key and skips an agent that already has a live key there. Each target's own signature check must accept a key-adding commit signed by the factory key (a one-off change in that repository, by a key already listed there or by Dinis).
key-apply.source: Dinis, 22 Nov 2026 13:39 UTC on the Decision Desk (relayed by conductor.d from maestro.d's session): "I like factory doing it because that leaves a full track record and if infrastructure as code, but the factory agent should merge it after a security review. For tasks like this I should not be the bottleneck"; in factory.d's session ~15:30 UTC: "build the factory [signed] key ... every time you do here, you should also do a security check and role-based security checks".
key-apply.reviews_note: Each key request needs one review per role listed in limits.reviews, as keys/<date>__<id>/review.<role>.json: committed and signed by an agent of that role, naming the exact request commit, with its verdict (pass, fail or needs-a-person), what it checked and what it did or asks (actions). The requester and every reviewer are different agents in different roles. Only all-pass applies; needs-a-person waits for Dinis or a lawyer, recorded in a new review. Each review's checks and actions are printed in the run summary and quoted in the commit that adds the key. Counsel checks, one line each: licences of what is used; consent of anyone named; personal data and privacy; third parties' names and terms; our own policies. Counsel flags and records; it does not decide the law. Dinis, 22 Nov 2026 ~16:35 UTC in factory.d's session: "Yes, you should have reviews for those key requests where you should have security and counsel. I agree. And then report if there was any actions."; earlier: "we always want a position where we never knowingly break a law or break a requirement or break a license".

keys_rule: Each agent publishes its own key when it starts: its first commit to this repository adds one entry to team/keys.json, its own (agent and session as the commit's Agent: and Claude-Session: trailers, status active, with bundle.sign), changes nothing else there, and is signed by that new key; build/check-signatures.mjs verifies that one commit against the key it adds, and every later commit against its parent's keys. One live key per agent name: a second session of a role takes its own name, <role>.<label>.<account>@SovereignWebsite.dinis (for example conductor.keys.d@SovereignWebsite.dinis), while there is only one <role>.<account>. An agent may retire its own entry; a conductor (an agent whose may_change lists team/keys.json) may also retire another agent's entry. No commit adds another agent's key, edits a key, name or session in place, or removes an entry; changing another agent's key is Dinis's. build/abp.mjs keysChange enforces this. Trade-off, accepted by Dinis: anyone with push on dev can publish a key under an unused name, so the trust rests on the team's GitHub write access and the session trailer.
